author: LeoHeller
title: smoke_AvgPoolV14CeilTorch CPU test fails on ACL primitive type mismatch (undef_f32 vs acl_f32)
signature: primType is unexpected undef_f32 Expected acl_f32|Flaky Test

failed_jobs.name: CPU functional tests / CPU functional tests
failed_jobs.symptom: 1 of 72267 smoke tests failed: AvgPoolingV14LayerCPUTest expected ACL primitive but got undef primitive

failed_jobs.name: ci/gha_overall_status_linux_arm64
failed_jobs.symptom: Aggregated workflow status reported failure due to the CPU functional tests job failure

key_errors:
src/plugins/intel_cpu/tests/functional/utils/cpu_test_utils.cpp:248: Failure
Value of: primTypeCheck(primType)
  Actual: false
Expected: true
primType is unexpected : undef_f32 Expected : acl_f32
root_cause: This is a known recurring flaky-test pattern on the ARM64 CPU plugin: the AvgPooling/related layer tests assert that the executed primitive implementation is the ACL (Arm Compute Library) kernel (primType == acl_f32), but on this run the CPU plugin's implementation-selection logic non-deterministically picked the fallback 'undef' (reference/generic) implementation instead, failing the assertion in cpu_test_utils.cpp:248. This is unrelated to the PR under test (#38669), which only touches CMake regex-escaping logic for EXCLUDED_SOURCE_PATHS and does not touch the CPU plugin or its primitive-selection code at all. The same primType-mismatch signature (eb0b94c864ee1a85) has recurred 4 times previously across unrelated PRs since 2026-09-11, each time involving a different parametrized test instance of the same family of primitive-type assertions, confirming this is a pre-existing non-deterministic test/plugin issue rather than something introduced by this PR.
reproduction_steps: Not reliably reproducible locally since it is a flaky/non-deterministic primitive-selection outcome. To attempt reproduction: build OpenVINO for ARM64 with CPU plugin and ACL enabled, then repeatedly run `ov_cpu_func_tests --gtest_filter=*smoke_AvgPoolV14CeilTorch_CPU_4D*AvgPoolingV14LayerCPUTest*` until the primType mismatch reoccurs; may require many iterations since it only manifested once in ~72k smoke tests this run.
recommended_actions: No action needed on PR #38669 — this failure is unrelated to the CMake changes being merged.
Investigate CPU plugin primitive-selection logic for AvgPooling on ARM64/ACL builds to determine why it occasionally falls back to the reference ('undef') implementation instead of acl_f32.

Consider loosening the test assertion to tolerate an occasional fallback-to-reference implementation when the ACL kernel does not support the given parameter combination, or add retry/quarantine for this specific parametrized test family.
Re-run the failed CPU functional tests job; it is expected to pass on retry given the non-deterministic nature of the failure.
prevention_strategies: Track recurring primType-mismatch flaky tests in a dedicated ticket and consider marking the specific parametrized AvgPoolingV14LayerCPUTest / MatMulDecompressConvertTest instances as known-flaky (disabled_tests.log) until the underlying ACL primitive-selection non-determinism is fixed, to avoid repeatedly blocking unrelated merge-queue PRs.
historical_context: Same signature (primType is unexpected ... Expected acl_f32 | Flaky Test, hash eb0b94c864ee1a85) previously recorded 4 times between 2026-09-11 and 2026-10-02 across PRs #37783, #37885, #38052, #38528, none of which touched CPU plugin primitive-selection code. A related but distinct signature (76751669c7a78fcd, 'primType is unexpected unknown Expected ref') was also seen once on PR #36890 in 2026-07-17, suggesting a broader family of primType-assertion flakiness in the CPU test suite.
